subject: Cooking
title: Stone Milling vs. Roller Milling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Stone Milling vs. Roller Milling.

hook.text: In 1878, the roller mill was invented — and bread was never the same. Neither was human nutrition.

buildup.text: Stone mills crush the entire grain — bran, germ, and endosperm — producing nutritious whole-grain flour.

discovery.text: Roller mills separate the components, discarding bran and germ to produce pure white endosperm flour.

twist.text: White flour lost most B vitamins, iron, and fiber — causing beriberi and pellagra epidemics by the early 1900s.

climax.text: Governments mandated flour 'enrichment' — adding back the nutrients that milling had stripped away.

punchline.text: We remove nutrition, then add it back. And call it progress.

quiz.question: What health consequence followed the adoption of roller milling?
options: Vitamin deficiency diseases like beriberi and pellagra

details.summary: Stone milling crushes grain between two stones, keeping the germ, bran, and endosperm together. Roller milling separates these components through sequential steel rollers, producing white flour stripped of nutrients.
details.whyItMatters: The roller milling revolution created the modern white flour that dominates baking. It also caused widespread nutritional deficiency that led to mandatory flour enrichment laws still in effect today.
takeaways: Stone milling retains germ and bran with all their nutrients
Roller mills separate components to produce pure white endosperm
Nutrient loss from roller milling led to mandatory enrichment laws

faq.question: Why did roller milling replace stone milling?
faq.answer: Roller mills process grain faster, at higher volume, and produce consistent white flour that stores longer because removing the oily germ prevents rancidity. White flour was seen as pure and modern. Consumer demand for white bread drove the transition despite nutritional costs.

faq.question: What nutrients are lost in roller-milled white flour?
faq.answer: Roller milling removes B vitamins, iron, fiber, vitamin E, healthy fats, and minerals concentrated in the bran and germ. Enrichment adds back some B vitamins and iron but not fiber, vitamin E, or most minerals. Whole grain flour retains everything that roller milling strips away.
